summary: Jerzy Bańczerowski studied linguistics at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (~1956–1961). He became head of its Department of General and Comparative Linguistics in 1969, served as professor there (1977–1991), and was a member of the Polish Academy of Sciences.

Jerzy Kuryłowicz studied at the University of Lviv (~1913–1923) and under Antoine Meillet (~1923–1925). A scholar of linguistics and Indology, he held posts at the University of Lviv (~1927–1941) and Jagiellonian University (~1946–1965).

Jessie Pons works in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed a doctoral thesis at Paris-Sorbonne University by 2011 and was attested as a Junior Professor at Ruhr University Bochum in 2019.
Jesung Woo, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, earned a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania. He held an attested post at Dongguk University (2001–2003).
Jey Flick, active in Indology and Buddhist studies, studied under Sheldon Pollock (attested 1984–2007) and held a post at the University of California, Berkeley.
Jian Ouyang was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Yang Renshan (~1904–1911). He founded the China Institute of Inner Learning and served as its head (~1922–1943).

Jiang Wu completed graduate studies at Nankai and Harvard (attested 2002), studying under Tu Weiming, Robert M. Gimello, Peter K. Bol, and Zhichao Chen. A scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology, he was professor at the University of Arizona (attested 2011–2018).
Jianming Hu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (attested 2015). In 2015, he was also attested as a researcher at Komazawa University.

Jiayao An studied under Su Bai (~1979–1982) in the fields of archaeology and sinology. Around 1982, she was appointed a special researcher and Xi'an laboratory director at the Institute of Archaeology, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
Jien Abe studied Buddhist studies and Indology as a graduate student at the University of Tokyo (attested 1973). He served as a professor at Meiji University until 2001.

Jigdal Dagchen Sakya, active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied under Ngawang Thutop Wangchuk, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dilgo Khyentse. He held a post at the University of Washington (~1960–1963).

Jigme Chhoeda studied at Druk Sangag Choeling and Tango monasteries under several traditional teachers. In Tibetology and Buddhist studies, his posts include abbot of Tango Monastery (~1986–1990), Drapoi Lopen (1986–1990), and Dorji Lopen (1995) at the Central Monastic Body.
Jigme Chökyi Sengge, active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studied under Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje and Dilgo Khyentse.
Jigme Pema Wangchen is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Dzi Gar Khenpo Nor Yang, Drukpa Khenpo Ngawang Chödrak, and Mi-pham-bśad-sgrub-chos-kyi-ñin-byed-mchog.
Jigme Tenpai Nyima studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Jigmeth Junu, a scholar in Buddhist studies, earned an MA at Fo Guang University (attested 2013) under the supervision of Yongdong Shi, and also studied under Hui Xian.
Jikai Fujiyoshi was a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Rissho University and was attested as a member at Kyoto University in 1967.

Jikido Takasaki studied at the University of Tokyo and Pune University. In Buddhist studies and Indology, he taught at Komazawa, Tokyo (professor 1977–1987), and Waseda, and served as president of Tsurumi University (1992–2004).

Jim G. Shaffer earned his BA at Arizona State University (~1961–1965) and his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1972). Working in archaeology and Indology, he became a professor of anthropology at Case Western Reserve University (~1979).

Jim Rheingans, working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earned an MA from the University of Hamburg and a PhD from the University of the West of England/Bath Spa University, supervised by David P. Jackson, Mahinda Deegalle, and Fiona Montgomery.
